1. Case 1: Antibiotic hepatotoxicity
The patient developed abdominal pain, nausea, and fatigue weeks after oral antibiotic treatment, with hepatomegaly and leg edema. Laboratory tests show a cholestatic enzyme pattern (elevated ALP, AST, GGT, and INR with normal ALT/bilirubin), negative viral hepatitis serology, and leukocytosis, all supporting drug-induced liver injury. The strong temporal link to antibiotics further favors this diagnosis. The absence of a monoclonal component on serum protein electrophoresis reduces the likelihood of smoldering myeloma progression. Autoimmune hepatic flare remains possible but is less likely given the predominantly cholestatic pattern and lack of autoimmune serology results. Therefore, antibiotic hepatotoxicity is the most probable diagnosis.
